title: Israeli Tourists Have a Bad Reputation Around the World
author: Kenn Maurice
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/a-c-
uk_Qw2GvTe4-unsplash.jpg)

Photograph Source: A. C. for Unsplash+

In May, 2025, a restaurant worker in Thailand asked an Israeli tourist to
remove her shoes before entering the establishment, a traditional cultural
custom in the country. The tourist refused to take off her shoes, shouting,
"My money helps build your country." Everything was caught on a video which
went viral.

The incident sparked a debate about the open secret of rudeness and aggression
rife in Israeli tourists abroad. A discussion long forbidden, as most who even
hinted at the phenomenon were tarred as antisemitic for suggesting this. But
since the onset of Israel's campaign of annihilation in Gaza, its violent
pogroms in the occupied West Bank, ethnic cleansing in southern Lebanon and
unprovoked war against Iran, reservations have greatly eased throughout the
world.

The reality is that there are scores of reports of Israelis behaving in this
manner in the countries they visit. From vandalism to disrespect of local
customs to violent confrontations, from Sri Lanka to Brazil to Thailand to
Chile to the Netherlands, Israelis have a bad reputation due to an enormous
amount of incidents that have piled up over the years. And this has only
worsened since the onset of Israel's genocidal campaign in Gaza.

The Maccabee riots in Amsterdam in 2024 highlighted much of this backlash
against these incidents. Gangs of Israeli football fans rampaged throughout
the city, chanting "death to Arabs" and singing gleefully about dead children
in Gaza, ripping down Palestinian flags off of private homes and businesses,
and attacking people they believed were Arab or Palestinian. The Israeli
government and political organizations which support the apartheid regime were
quick to accuse those who protested or even talked about this aggression as
being antisemitic. But the video evidence proved otherwise.

Antisemitism is an odious and dangerous social hatred. It should always be
condemned. But the state of Israel and its supporters have weaponized the term
by equating the nation-state of Israel and the supremacist political ideology
of Zionism with the ethnic and religious identity of Judaism. Thus, any
condemnation of Israel or Zionism is erroneously painted as antisemitic.

It is important to look at this phenomenon, not through the lens of Jewish
identity, but the impact of colonialism, national arrogance and racist
ideologies on a society. Israelis are not unique in this regard. There are
other countries which have a similar bad reputation thanks to this historical
context.

Americans, for example, have also become a global pariah due to the
belligerent imperialism of their government, its support for genocide, and
their nationalistic chauvinism. Unsurprisingly, it also has a long legacy
rooted in dispossession, oppression and genocide. And visitors to the US, as
well as Israel, have long reported mistreatment by customs and border
agencies, further tarnishing their reputation abroad.

As Israel becomes more and more isolated and loathed in the court of public
opinion, Israelis have found they are less welcome in the places they once
holidayed in. The boycott of Eurovision by five European nations due to
Israel's participation is a real world consequence of this growing disgust
with the crimes of that state.

But instead of grappling with the implications and facing the racist character
of its state, many Israelis are defaulting to the false notion that they are
hated simply because they are Jewish. Ironically, this belief in perpetual
victimhood and refusal to challenge the racism rife in their society and the
apartheid, ethnic cleansing and genocide perpetrated by their government, will
only serve to isolate them even more.
